subject: dynamically expand / contract a directed graph

messages.author: 240fe1a61c9c46b9
messages.subject: dynamically expand / contract a directed graph
parts:
Hello,


I have some questions about the best way to make a dynamically

expandable/contractable directed graph.  See below for specifics.


I am a newbie to visNetwork and Shiny.  I have searched various

resources and have not quite found what I am looking for.


I explain what I mean by "expandable/contractable directed graph" with

the following example:


Suppose I have a directed graphical model - a taxonomy such as the following:


-- Animal

---- Fish

---- Amphibian

---- Mammal

------ Dog

------ Cat

------ Dolphin


One way I can simply and beautifully display this with visNetwork is

as follows:


require(visNetwork, quietly = TRUE)

visNetwork(dot = 'dinetwork {"Animal" -> "Mammal" ; "Animal" ->

        "Fish"; "Animal" ->"Amphibian"; "Mammal" -> "Dog"; "Mammal" ->

        "Cat"; "Mammal" -> "Dolphin"}', width = "100%") Fish Amphibian


There are, of course, other ways to display this with visNetwork too.

Whatever.


I simply want to be able to click on a node in graph like the above

visNetwork graph and have it expand / contract (or show and hide)

dynamically.  


Let me make this as clear as possible with an example:


Suppose I have the above graph displayed and I click on "Animal". At

that point the entire graph should disappear except for the node

"Animal".


Next I click on "Animal" again and the immediate outgoing neigbhoors

appear (i.e. nodes for "Fish", "Amphibian", "Mammal").


Next I click on "Mammal" and its immediate outgoing neighboors appear

(i.e. nodes for "Dog", "Cat", "Dolphin").


Next I click on "Mammal" again its immediate outgoing neighboors

disappear.


...Thats an example of what I mean by "have a graph expand and

contract dynamically" or to put it another way to "show and hide

dynamically."


KEY QUESTIONS:


(1) Is there a pre-existing code snippet / module in visNetwork and/or

Shiny someone can point out?


(2) Alternatively, do you have any guidance on how I might roll my

own?  E.g. can I / should I just do this entirely in visNetwork or am

I better off coming up to speed on Shiny as well as visNetwork.  Are

there particular functions / methods etc you recommend I look at?


Thanks very much!


Bill
